Theme

Kitchen, meals & drinks

may it turn out well phrase

also it’s in the oven

classical

Verg. Ecl. 8, 106, via Ranieri

Bonum sit!

Said as the dish goes into the oven.

Examples

  • Utramque in furnum mīsērunt. «Bonum sit!» inquit pater.

    They put both in the oven. “May it turn out well!” said Dad.Libellus IV, Diēs Grātulātiōnis

  • Ēn erit umquam ille diēs?

    Will that day ever come? (for waiting at the oven)Verg. Ecl. 8, 7–8

See also be hungry.

SourcesThese are quotations, and their sources are given. Libellī II and IV and the back-matter lists of “locī memoriā tenendī” suggest when to use them with Theo.

Theodōrus et pater · Ad Larem avītum, Libellī I–VII, as they stood on 7 November 2026, with their glosses. Examples marked “Libellus” quote those texts word for word; classical passages are cited by author.
